Messages.Author: John Flournoy
Messages.Body:
kula...@gmail.com wrote:
> Vampire plays Martial Ritus on a younger vampire...
>
> The younger vampire plays Descent into Darkness...
>
> It's out of play till next turn... When he(she?) comes back up, the
> next untap has past... Those the Martial Ritus ever burn then?

The younger vampire goes out of play, and so does the Martial Ritus.

When he returns to play, there is a Martial Ritus in play with the text
"During your next untap phase, burn this card." So on the next untap
(assuming it doesn't leave play again), it burns.

Since it was out of play during your first 'next untap', it never
notices that it missed one, and triggers at the first (following)
opportunity once it returns to play.

> Same goes for :
> Khabar: Glory?
> Psychic Projection?
> Sleep Unseen?

The same for each (although PP burns during 'your untap phase', not
even your 'next', it's still waiting for the first instance while in
play.)

The same general rule would hold true if you temporarily left play via
other means, like being Banished.

(There's rulings by LSJ on this: try searching on 'Baltimore Purge' and
'out of play'.)

>
> Sleep unseen seems too cool of a combo... =D
>
> Play decent into darkness, and if the action is successful.

If the DiD action succeeds, she's out of play and can't play Sleep
Unseen.

-John Flournoy

No. When you get to your (next) unatp phase, you burn it.

> fixed once played?

No. Effects from the play of the card are fixed when played.
Effects from the card in play are evaluated when used.
See Army of Rats and what happens after you oust your first prey.

Messages.Author: Chris Berger
Messages.Body:
kula...@gmail.com wrote:
>
> Real world Example...
>
> You have to throw away your trash into the next bin. The next bin
> isn't there at the moment. That doesn't mean the following bin is
> where the trash should go.
>

Which is the next bin and which is the following bin? I don't
understand. Why not just throw your trash into whichever bin is
available? Is there a chance it might get mixed in with the other
trash and then you can't tell whose trash is whose?

Here's a different example:

I need to take the #2 bus downtown. Of course, I want the *next* #2
bus that comes along - I'm in a rush. So, I'm waiting at the bus stop.
If the #2 bus comes, I get on it - I don't worry that it's no longer
the "next" #2 bus once it's arrived. On the other hand, if I really
have to take a pee and I run off into the nearest building, when I come
out, I will wait on the bench for the *next* #2 bus. This is
regardless of whether or not another #2 bus came by in the meantime.
As far as I'm concerned, I didn't see if a bus passed while I was in
the bathroom, so any buses that stopped then don't exist for me, and
I'm still waiting for the next bus to come.
